newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures await fresh U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures await fresh U.S. data.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were slightly down in late lacklustre dealings as the market awaited U.S. economic data on Tuesday, traders said.
At 1600 GMT, DTB March Bund futures were down seven basis points at 101.12 points and were stuck in a 22-point range as the market consolidated after last week's turbulence.
The benchmark 10-year cash Bund was trading at 101.52 with a yield of 5.79 percent, slightly down from last Friday's closing price of 101.61.
"There is not much going on," said one Frankfurt trader. "People are waiting for the U.S data on Tuesday."

Slated for release on Tuesday at 1330 GMT is U.S. fourth quarter employment costs, seen in a Reuter consensus survey rising 1.2 percent, and also the consumer confidence survey information at 1500 GMT.
Both reports were expected to have an impact on how the Federal Reserve debates its interest rate policy and traders looked for stable dealings ahead of the data.

A lack of fresh domestic news also kept the German market focused on the U.S., including little reaction on Monday to provisional west German consumer prices for January rising 1.8 percent year-on-year.

Traders said the market had already factored in the German inflation data based on the shock value last week of the higher-than-expected inflation data from the four west German states used to compute the national data.
On a technical basis, traders looked for March futures to face support at 100.30 and 100.20, while resistance was pegged at 101.50 as a limit for any upward near-term movement.
